newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen up on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen up on Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares fell for the third session running and analysts said that after a likely rise on Wednesday, signalled by stronger buying after fixing, a slight downtrend could last to September's parliamentary elections.
Analysts said a slight downtrend seemed likely as Poland geared up for the September 21 vote and counted costs of recent flooding, which swamped more than one percent of the country.

"It seems the most important (negative) role is the increased risk linked with the polls -- maybe if prices fall significantly players will take the risk linked with the vote and buy," said Mateusz Andrzejewski of Bank Pekao SA house.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.6 percent to 15,135 points and turnover eased 3.8 percent to 164.6 million zlotys ($47.6 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 44 to 38 with 24 stocks flat.

On Tuesday a deputy economy minister said Polish firms suffered property losses of about five billion zlotys ($1.4 million) as a result of flooding, a figure analysts said would likely not encouraging buying.

Builders were seen benefiting from reconstruction effforts but analysts said government plans to take up to 2.5 billion zlotys in central bank loans for flood relief could speed inflation, cause rate rises and curb bourse growth.
They said food producer Pekpol fell 8.8 percent after a newspaper reported on Tuesday that the firm would revise down its 1997 net profit forecast later in July.

Analysts said tyre maker Stomil Olsztyn, down 4.5 percent, was hurt by June net loss data published late last week which followed its late-June announcement it would make provisions that month due to a recall of two defective tyre types.
